category_title: Timid students developing voice through co-teaching
minimal_context: Brandon is standing in front of the science classroom to co-teach a lesson to his peers.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Brandon, it is time for you to stand in front of the class and co-teach the science lesson.

STUDENT: Okay. I want to do this because I'm in front of all of these people it seems like they trust me and chose me to do something smart.

TUTOR: Go ahead and start.

STUDENT: I usually feel like I have no voice in here because my partner doesn't like to talk to me, so I will try to stand in front of people and talk.

TUTOR: What is the first part of the science content?

STUDENT: (Appears very timid and nervous speaking in front of a class full of his peers) The... first... part... is... (talking slow and quietly)...

options.A: Create a seating arrangement in groups so that the student can always be a part of one of the peer groups during the science lesson.
options.B: Frame the student as a 'researcher helping scientists' during the science lesson, justifying mundane tasks by comparing them to professional scientific standards.
options.C: Provide noncontingent attention to the student throughout the day, and ignore any problem behaviors that function to gain attention during the science lesson.
options.D: Provide the science lesson plan for homework. Review it with the student to ensure content accuracy, and have the student enhance the lesson plan to reflect their own teaching style.
